data.risk: Coface C / business climate C (Oct 2025); Allianz Trade "sensitive". UGX at 4,138/USD (13 Oct 2026), inflation 4.6% (Sep 2026). Landlocked: depends on Mombasa; Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb attacks in Jul–Sep 2026 raise freight and war-risk premiums. Use LC/CAD or ECGE credit insurance for new buyers.
data.scoreBasis: Small market (49.6M pop, ~$62B GDP; chocolate imports only ~$4M, food preps 2106 ~$16M in 2023). Egypt already ships $115.9M (2025) and is #3 chocolate supplier (14.2%). COMESA 0% neutralises Kenya's EAC advantage if the CoO is right. Gaps: no visible whipping-powder, fillings or cake-mix brand online; Rich's (Kookee) and Puratos (from Kenya) are the main pros. Minus: PVoC cost, landlocked logistics via Bab el-Mandeb, Coface C payment risk.
data.tariffNote: COMESA FTA: Egypt-origin goods 0% in Uganda (applied since 23 Mar 2015) with a correctly signed COMESA certificate of origin (Kuku Foods v URA, 2024). Without it: EAC CET 25–35%, and Uganda FY2026/27 stays at 60% on 1806.90 bread spreads and 20.07 jams, 35% on 1901.20.90 bakery mixes. Whether those national rates override COMESA 0% is unverified — confirm with URA. Plus VAT 18%, WHT 6%, infrastructure levy 1.5%, IDF 1%.
